nodes.description: A heterozygous missense substitution in the ALK tyrosine kinase domain is present in every cell from conception. The recurrent alleles reported in neuroblastoma families - R1275Q, G1128A, R1192P and T1151M/T1151R - all lie in the kinase domain. No germline truncating, frameshift, splice or whole-gene deletion allele causes this syndrome: the mechanism is gain of function, so loss-of-function alleles are not causal.

nodes.description: The dominant manifestation and the reason the syndrome is clinically important. Risk is highest in infancy and falls through childhood. Multifocal and bilateral primary tumors are the hallmark that should raise suspicion of a germline ALK variant: all three germline variants in the French series arose in multifocal cases, against a background rate of 3-4% bilateral or multifocal primaries among neuroblastoma patients generally. There is no HPO term for multifocal primary neuroblastoma, so that feature is carried here rather than bound.

nodes.description: Sympathetic ganglia and the adrenal medulla carry an enlarged, persistently undifferentiated neuroblast population beyond the normal developmental window. An activating Alk allele at the endogenous mouse locus produces this on its own, and MYCN overexpression drives the same hyperplasia, so the germline allele and the cooperating somatic lesion both feed it. It is the permissive state of the carrier rather than a tumor: about half of carriers never develop a neuroblastic tumor at all, and tumor risk falls through childhood. What becomes of the pool in an unaffected human carrier is not reported - no study follows sympathoadrenal tissue in carriers - so this entry states the penetrance and the age gradient and does not claim that the hyperplasia regresses.
